transcript.user: Do I need Self Assessment if I started freelancing?
transcript.assistant:
Yes, if you started freelancing and earned income from it, you will likely need to register for Self Assessment. You must register by 5 October following the end of the tax year in which you started freelancing. For the 2025-26 tax year, if you began freelancing in that year, you would need to register by 5 October 2026. 

Have you already registered for Self Assessment?

transcript.user: Simple income, first time — cheapest suitable package?
transcript.assistant:
For simple income and first-time filing, the lowest suitable package is the **Self Assessment Simple** for £119 per tax year. This package is designed for straightforward tax situations. 

You can find more details and register [here](https://www.taxsimba.co.uk/self-assessment). Would you like assistance with anything else?

transcript.user: My qualifying income was £55,000 in 2024-25. Do I need MTD from April 2026?
transcript.assistant:
Yes — if your qualifying income was more than £50,000 for 2024-25, you need to use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax from 6 April 2026. Qualifying income means self-employment and property income before expenses (turnover/gross), not profit.

Official guidance: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/find-out-if-and-when-you-need-to-use-making-tax-digital-for-income-tax

transcript.user: What is the lowest suitable Simbian plan if I am in scope?
transcript.assistant:
The lowest suitable Simbian plan for you, if you are in scope for Making Tax Digital, is **Simbian Comply** at £29.99 per month (VAT included). This plan includes Xero Simple and covers the requirements for MTD.

You can find more details and register here: [Simbian Comply](https://www.taxsimba.co.uk/making-tax-digital).

transcript.user: My affairs involve trusts, overseas income and crypto — can SIMBA file everything?
transcript.assistant:
TaxSimba primarily focuses on Self Assessment tax returns and Making Tax Digital services. While we can assist with Self Assessment, including income from various sources, we do not handle complex areas like trusts or specific overseas income reporting directly. For crypto, we can help with the relevant tax implications under Self Assessment.

For comprehensive advice tailored to your situation, including trusts and overseas income, I recommend consulting with a qualified accountant. Would you like to know more about our Self Assessment packages?
